items.question: Check 3 (a), literal: does the planted subset activate in >= 90 % of the one-coupling Markov runs whose final kl_true < 0.01, in each training context? And how many runs reach kl_true < 0.01 at all?
items.definition_used: Runs: markov-v1, the 10 one-coupling sets x {chain, iid}, every seed of the sky (202 runs: chain 102, iid 100; 1,2,3:1.0 chain has 12 seeds). Final kl_true = last value of the light curve's x_kl_true (step 30,000; measured on the test split of the run's own train_context). 'Activates' = the planted subset {x[t-l], l in L} + {xhat} has an event of kind 'activation' in ri_events (identical to detect_events(curve, alpha=0.01) for all 202 runs), left-censored activations included. Plausible alternatives: (a2) Amendment 1 C's onset rule, a (re)activation that is not left-censored and at whose checkpoint the planted Fourier coefficient has the sign of its final value; (a3) the planted subset is active at the end of training. 'Reach kl_true < 0.01 at all' = any light-curve point below 0.01.
items.literal_result: chain: 102 of 102 runs with final kl_true < 0.01 have a planted activation; iid: 100 of 100; pooled 202 of 202. Final kl_true < 0.01 in 102 of 102 chain and 100 of 100 iid runs; kl_true < 0.01 reached at some point in 102 of 102 chain and 100 of 100 iid runs, i.e. every seed of every coupling set (per-set counts and first crossing steps in by_coupling_context). Largest final kl_true: chain 0.00270, iid 0.00249 nats.
items.amended_result: Not changed by Amendment 1. Alternatives give the same counts: (a2) C-rule chain 102 of 102, iid 100 of 100; (a3) active at the end: chain 102 of 102, iid 100 of 100.

items.interpretation: The instrument finds the planted coupling in every converged run of both contexts; check 3 (a) passes. The kl_true conditioning removes nothing: every run converged.
items.caveats: 7 runs (all order 2, coupling sets 1:1.0 and 1:0.5) have a left-censored first planted activation at step 0: the untrained network's planted-pair RI is significant there with the wrong sign (Amendment 1 C). Each goes extinct by step 8 and re-activates with the right sign by step 15, so the C-rule alternative gives the same counts: 1:1.0 chain seed 0 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 3, 12]; f(step 0) = -0.065), 1:1.0 chain seed 9 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 8, 15]; f(step 0) = -0.118), 1:1.0 iid seed 9 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 6, 12]; f(step 0) = -0.118), 1:0.5 chain seed 0 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 3, 10]; f(step 0) = -0.065), 1:0.5 chain seed 9 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 7, 14]; f(step 0) = -0.118), 1:0.5 iid seed 0 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 3, 10]; f(step 0) = -0.065), 1:0.5 iid seed 9 (kinds activation/extinction/reactivation at steps [0, 7, 14]; f(step 0) = -0.118).

items.question: Check 3 (b), literal: does a non-planted subset with peak RI >= 10 x min_effect occur in <= 5 % of the one-coupling runs, in each training context?
items.definition_used: Non-planted = every stored subset other than the planted one; every Markov curve stores all n_candidates scanned subsets (xhat plus 1 to max_order - 1 lags; checked for 202 of 202 runs). Peak RI = max over all 60 checkpoints (step 0 included) of the stored bias-corrected RI; threshold 10 x min_effect = 0.01 nats (min_effect = 0.001 in every run). Denominator: all one-coupling runs of the context (plausible alternative: runs with final kl_true < 0.01; identical here). Alternative peak: peak_ri of a non-planted (re)activation event, which also requires q <= 0.01. 95 % bootstrap CIs (2,000 resamples, seed 20261112) resample seeds within coupling set, or coupling sets.
items.literal_result: chain: 36 of 102 runs (35.3 %, CI 31.4-39.2 % over seeds, 11.0-62.5 % over coupling sets); by set {'1,2,3,5:1.0': 10, '1,2,3:1.0': 12, '1,2,4:1.0': 1, '1,3:0.5': 1, '1,3:1.0': 3, '1:1.0': 9}. iid: 0 of 100 (largest non-planted peak 0.00969 nats, the initialisation offset). Pooled 36 of 202. The event-based peak and the kl-conditioned denominator give the same counts.
items.amended_result: Superseded by (c) (Amendment 1 B, which decides): see check3c.

items.interpretation: The registered peak criterion fails for chain training and passes for iid training. The failures are real interactions learned transiently from the chain's correlated contexts (result_chain_transients), not instrument noise: iid twins with the same initial weights and probes stay below the bar. Amendment 1 B anticipated exactly this and replaced the criterion.
items.caveats: The untrained network's RI reaches 0.0092 nats at step 0 (on {x[t-5], xhat}, seed 7, identical in chain and iid twins), just below the 0.01 bar; one chain run (1,3:0.5 seed 7) crosses the bar only through that offset (0.0101 at step 2). Without it the chain count is 35 of 102; the verdict is unchanged.

items.question: Check 3 (c), Amendment 1 B (decides): at the end of training, is the largest non-planted RI over the last five checkpoints <= 10 x min_effect in >= 95 % of runs, in both contexts?
items.definition_used: Per run: max over all stored non-planted subsets and over the last five checkpoints (steps 15,623, 17,800, 20,282, 26,330 and 30,000) of the bias-corrected RI; a run passes if it is <= 0.01 nats. Plausible alternatives: max over subsets of the per-subset mean over the last five checkpoints; the final checkpoint only.
items.literal_result: (the registered criterion is (b), reported in check3b)
items.amended_result: chain: 102 of 102 runs pass (largest value 0.00144 nats, on {x[t-3], xhat}); iid: 100 of 100 (largest 0.00157). Alternatives: mean over the last five chain 102 of 102, iid 100 of 100; final checkpoint chain 102 of 102, iid 100 of 100.

items.interpretation: Every chain-induced interaction has vanished by the end of training: the largest late non-planted RI is 1.6 x min_effect, far below the 10 x bar, in both contexts. With (a) passing, check 3 passes under the amended (deciding) definition.
items.caveats: The margin is wide, so max versus mean over the last five checkpoints does not matter.

items.question: Check 3 overall (Markov instrument check): (a) together with the non-planted criterion.
items.definition_used: Literal = (a) and (b); amended = (a) and (c); Amendment 1 B states that the amended one decides. Each evaluated per training context.
items.literal_result: (a) passes in both contexts; (b) chain 36 of 102 -> fail, iid 0 of 100 -> pass. Literal check 3: fails (chain), passes (iid).
items.amended_result: (a) passes; (c) chain 102 of 102, iid 100 of 100. Amended check 3: passes in both contexts.

(b) chain 36 of 102, iid 0 of 100
(c) chain 102 of 102, iid 100 of 100
items.interpretation: No sign of a bug or a mis-set threshold: iid runs pass every version; chain runs fail only the peak version, because of real, transient, chain-induced interactions, which Amendment 1 B re-classified as a result.
items.caveats: Sanity checks behind all three: tycho imported from the repository; every curve has 60 checkpoints ending at the 30,000-step budget; the planted subset is stored and named in the ground truth of every curve; the final planted coefficient is positive in every run (median 0.999 x tanh(beta)); events table = detect_events recomputation in every run; step-0 RI identical in chain/iid twins.

items.question: Which non-planted interactions do chain-trained one-coupling runs learn transiently (subsets, runs, peak RI and step, rise and decay relative to the planted onset, iid twins), and do the chain's statistics explain them?
items.definition_used: Transient = a non-planted stored subset whose RI reaches 10 x min_effect = 0.01 nats in a chain run. Rise = its first activation event (detect_events, alpha 0.01; the event step is the first of the two confirming checkpoints) and its first checkpoint >= 0.01; decay = its first extinction event after the peak (RI < min_effect/2 on two consecutive checkpoints). Planted onset = Amendment 1 C onset (first non-left-censored (re)activation with the final sign). Timing differences in checkpoint indices of the 60-point log grid. iid twin = same coupling set and seed trained on iid contexts (same initial weights and probes; seeds 10 and 11 of 1,2,3:1.0 have none). 'Initialisation-level' = peak within the first three checkpoints with >= 90 % of it already at step 0. Chain statistics from the actual training corpus (MarkovLanguage, same config, data_seed 0, 199,994 windows): rho_A = E[s_t prod_(l in A) s_(t-l)]; analytic value tanh(beta)^|J| with e_u = s_u chi_L(u) i.i.d. of mean tanh(beta) and s_t chi_A = prod_(j in J) e_(t-j) (0 when no finite J exists); Bayes-optimal marginal predictor g_A(s_A) = E_chain[s_t | s_A], its Walsh coefficient and exact local RI of A + xhat under uniform probes (what a model predicting from the lags of A alone would show).

items.interpretation: Every chain-induced transient sits on a subset A whose lags correlate with x_t in the chain: with one coupling L, e_t = s_t chi_L(t) is i.i.d. with mean tanh(beta), so products of shifted copies of the planted pattern give E[s_t chi_A] = tanh(beta)^k (e.g. {1,2,3}: s_t s_(t-4) = e_t e_(t-1), tanh^2(1) = 0.58; {1}: lag l gives tanh^l; {1,2,3,5}: {4,5,6} and {1,2,4}: {3,4,5} give tanh^2; {1,3}: {4,5} and {2,6} give tanh^3). Simulation of the training corpus matches these values, and iid contexts have none (|rho| < 0.007). Two regimes: (1) where the shortcut is simpler than the planted term ({1,2,3}:1.0, a single lag against a 3-lag product) the model first learns almost the whole Bayes-optimal marginal predictor on x[t-4] (peak / marginal RI 0.79 to 0.96 (median 0.88)), which peaks 1 to 6 checkpoints before the planted onset in 12 of 12 runs and is unlearned once the planted term explains it (extinct at steps 2,206 to 6,267); (2) where the shortcut is not simpler ({1}, {1,3}, {1,2,4}, {1,2,3,5} at beta = 1) it grows alongside or after the planted term (early growth ratios dfA/dfL of the order of rho_A/rho_L), reaches only 6 to 20 % of the marginal-predictor RI (0.0105 to 0.0241 nats) and peaks after the planted onset (27 of 27), before vanishing by step 3,718. At beta = 0.5 and 0.8 the correlations (tanh^2(0.5) = 0.21) give marginal RIs <= 0.042 nats and no chain-induced transient reaches the bar. The iid twins, with no chain correlation (|rho| <= 0.0068), stay far below the bar on the same subsets (<= 0.0072 nats, the largest values being the shared step-0 offsets; <= 0.0057 from step 10 on).
items.caveats: The model's coefficient on A is a learning-dynamics quantity, so the Bayes-optimal marginal RI is an upper reference, not a prediction; the early-growth ratio dfA/dfL (stored per run) is only roughly tanh(beta)^(k-1) for the {1} set because lag 1 explains the others away while both grow. The 1,3:0.5 seed 7 and 1:1.0 seed 7 {x[t-5], xhat} crossings are initialisation-level (offset 0.0092 at step 0, same in the iid twin). Peak steps are limited by the 60-point log grid (adjacent checkpoints differ by factors up to 1.3).

items.question: Does the chain-induced transient delay the planted term? Planted onset with chain vs iid contexts for the same coupling set.
items.definition_used: Per coupling set, median planted onset over seeds per context and the ratio chain / iid of the medians, with a 95 % bootstrap CI (2,000 resamples, seeds resampled within each context independently, seed 20261112 + offsets). Onsets: (ii) Amendment 1 C (first (re)activation not left-censored with the final Fourier sign; primary, as for questions 4 to 6); (i) the registered first activation event (left-censored ones at step 0 included); (iii) the planted Fourier coefficient reaching 25 % of its population value tanh(beta) (Amendment 1 E's form; also 10 % and 50 % in the JSON). No run is censored.

items.interpretation: Only 1,2,3:1.0, the set whose transient is a strong first-order shortcut that peaks before the planted onset, shows a clear delay: the planted onset roughly doubles with chain contexts and the seed ranges do not overlap (C onset 162-273 vs 96-125 steps, as in the Amendment 1 pilot). A mechanism consistent with this: once the marginal predictor rho s_(t-4) is fitted, the squared-loss signal left for the planted term is E[(s_t - g) chi_L] / E[s_t chi_L] = 0.42 (= 1 - tanh^2(1)) of its full value. Where the transient rises after the planted onset (1,2,3,5:1.0, 1,2,4:1.0, 1,3:1.0) the RI onset is not delayed (C ratios 1.00, 1.00, 1.19, CIs include 1); the coefficient's 25 % crossing is at most one checkpoint later (E25 ratios 1.00, 1.29, 1.14). For 1:1.0 the coefficient-based onsets are about 1.3 x later with chain contexts (E25 CI [1.00, 1.64]), but RI onsets there are at the initialisation scale (<= 15 steps). Sets without chain-induced transients show C and E25 ratios of 0.83 to 1.11, all CIs including 1.
items.caveats: Chain and iid training differ in more than the transient (the whole context distribution changes), so the delay is attributed to the chain-induced shortcut by association across coupling sets and by the signal argument, not by an intervention. Within 1,2,3:1.0 chain runs, the size of the transient does not significantly predict the onset. Medians sit on a 60-point log grid (adjacent checkpoints differ by 1.14-1.3 x), so bootstrap CIs are coarse and can be degenerate (e.g. [1.29, 1.38]).
